exposure: cord blood folate receptor alpha autoantibodies (FRAbs)
cohort: The study included 23 mothers and 25 preterm infants (born at <=32 weeks GA or <=1500g) and 25 mother-term infant pairs (born at >=37 weeks GA).
finding: Pregnant women with positive folate receptor autoantibodies had 4.9 times higher odds of having preterm birth, suggesting FRAbs might contribute to preterm birth.
gest_age: preterm infants <=32 weeks, term infants >=37 weeks
